summary: Episodic p99 latency waves traced to continuous-batcher drain-timing jitter
description: Issue summary: StreamlineAI reported recurring 10-30s waves where p99 latency spikes 2-8x baseline and intermittent 504s occur. Impact: user-facing timeouts on short prompt workloads, elevated error budget burn for the Dedicated pool. Environment: prod-us-east Dedicated nodes running serving-runtime v2.8.1 with continuous-batcher enabled. Observed: p95 stable while p99 shows periodic stair-step waves; batch size histograms show transient increases in microbatch size followed by queuing. Suspected root cause: drain scheduling jitter in continuous-batcher that sometimes aligns badly with arrival patterns, producing delayed flushes and head-of-line blocking.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision a Dedicated pool with continuous-batcher enabled and default linger_ms=20
2) Emit steady low-rate short requests (mean token count ~22) from ~200 concurrent connections
observe p99 over 2-3 minute windows for episodic waves
3) Capture batcher.drain_delay_ms and batch_size histograms; compare boundaries of p99 waves to drain timer variance
4) As mitigation, route traffic to non-continuous flush path and confirm p99 reverts to baseline
logs: 2026-03-08T09:03:42Z batcher scheduled_drain id=0x1f8f delay_ms=2 jitter_ms=13 flush_size=6
investigation_notes: Support triage: confirmed traffic profile dominated by short sequences and periodic background bursts
SRE: p99 wave boundaries align with increased variance in batcher.drain_delay_ms histogram on 3 nodes
Perf Eng: reproduced locally with synthetic traffic and traced drift to scheduling behavior under OS scheduling delay
No resource saturation observed: GPU and CPU utilization steady; queues grow only during wave windows
Additional finding: batcher reschedule used system clock, allowing positive drift when host scheduling latency occurred

resolution: Hotfix applied: batcher drain scheduling migrated to monotonic timers and jitter algorithm corrected to avoid correlated delays. Emergency mitigation reduced default linger_ms to 6ms for Dedicated pools while canary validated. Rollout completed to us-east Dedicated pools on 2026-03-10 08:12 UTC. Monitoring showed p99 returned to baseline and 504s ceased. Follow-ups scheduled: per-customer batcher tuning knob, CI tests for timer drift, runbook updates and postmortem publication.
